sections.markdown:
# Accuracy and teaching notes

Do not teach the general seventy-mile-per-hour interstate maximum without current issuer/legal confirmation. Physical106 gives four-second merge space, two-second resulting gaps, three-second following advice and then four seconds doubled in bad weather; preserve the conflicting numerical guidance as debt rather than select a universal minimum. Wildlife horn advice conflicts across physical109–110; chasing-dog acceleration, skimming an animal and braking-release impact mechanics are withheld for safety review. Do not generalize the exit-lane advice into a ban on necessary emergency slowing. Headlight guidance on physical112 uses a block rather than physical80 exact distances; preserve the source-specific legal distances elsewhere. Trip-duration and distance averages do not establish a safe driving allowance. Dated wildlife collision totals and image-only layouts remain unasserted. [A01] [A02] [A03] [A04] [A05] [A06] [A07] [A08] [A09] [A10]
Memory cue, authored product policy: “Plan the exit, match the gap, keep space; rural does not mean risk-free”. The cue retrieves complete cited rules and does not replace their conditions.
Terminology: A deceleration lane provides room to slow after leaving through traffic. Open, closed and changing zones describe the availability and visibility of travel space.
Misconception to correct: Mainline drivers must make room for a merging car, or a missed exit justifies reversing. Entering traffic yields, and a missed exit requires continuing forward to a later interchange.
